verdicts.reading: Iran's nuclear standoff and regional role make 2007 a highly unstable year in the Middle East, with Iran at the centre.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D31 top risk: Iran-centred instability (escalating nuclear standoff, confrontation) materially occurs in calendar 2007 with documented effect.
verdicts.reason: The standoff escalated: UNSC Resolution 1747 tightened sanctions (24 Mar 2007) and Iran seized 15 Royal Navy personnel (23 Mar-4 Apr). But no military confrontation followed, and the December 2007 US NIE lowered tension; the 'most unstable year in two decades' centred on Iran did not occur in full.

evidence.title: UN Security Council Resolution 1747
evidence.shows: Unanimous tightening of sanctions on Iran; Iran refuses suspension; Israel threatens action.

evidence.title: 2007 Iranian seizure of Royal Navy personnel
evidence.shows: 15 UK personnel held 13 days, released 4 April 2007 without escalation.

verdicts.reading: Nigeria's April 2007 elections seriously strain its democratic system.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D31 top risk: the 2007 election is badly compromised (fraud, violence, contested legitimacy) in calendar 2007.
verdicts.reason: EU observers called the election not credible, among the worst they had seen, with fraud, violence and disenfranchisement; the opposition rejected the result. Power still passed civilian to civilian, but the stated challenge to democracy materialised.

evidence.title: 2007 Nigerian presidential election
evidence.shows: EU chief observer: process 'cannot be considered to be credible'; rigging, violence; Yar'Adua inaugurated 29 May 2007.

verdicts.reading: Iraq and US policy there are in bad shape, with a risk of state collapse and wider sectarian war in 2007.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D31 top risk: Iraq's state collapses or sectarian war widens in calendar 2007.
verdicts.reason: Violence stayed severe in the first half of 2007 (about 1,700 civilian deaths in May) and the government met only 3 of 18 benchmarks, but the state did not collapse and violence fell sharply after the surge and the Sadr ceasefire (about 500 civilian deaths in December). The bad shape materialised; collapse and wider war did not.

evidence.title: Iraq War troop surge of 2007
evidence.shows: Civilian deaths fell from >1,700 (May) to ~500 (Dec 2007); state did not collapse; GAO: 3 of 18 benchmarks met by Sept 2007.

verdicts.reading: Turkey's 2007 presidential and parliamentary elections expose divisions and test its stability.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D31 top risk: the 2007 elections produce a material political crisis in calendar 2007.
verdicts.reason: The presidential vote triggered a military 'e-memorandum' (27 Apr), mass secularist rallies of over a million, a Constitutional Court annulment, an early general election (22 Jul) and a referendum; Gul was elected only on 28 Aug.

evidence.title: 2007 Turkish presidential election
evidence.shows: E-memorandum, Republic protests, court annulment of first round, snap election, referendum.

verdicts.reading: Russia's petro-fuelled assertiveness and maneuvering ahead of the 2008 succession raise Russia-related risk in 2007.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D31 top risk: Russia's assertive foreign/energy posture and succession maneuvering produce documented effects in calendar 2007.
verdicts.reason: Putin's Munich speech (10 Feb 2007) rejected the unipolar order; Russia suspended the CFE Treaty (July 2007); Medvedev was named successor in December 2007 amid open succession maneuvering.

evidence.title: Munich speech of Vladimir Putin
evidence.shows: Speech marks turn in Russia-West relations; CFE suspension July 2007; Medvedev chosen as successor later in 2007.

verdicts.reading: Elite tension in China rises around the fall 2007 Party Congress as Hu consolidates power, creating political risk.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D31 top risk: elite conflict around the 17th Party Congress materially disrupts Chinese politics or policy in calendar 2007.
verdicts.reason: The 17th Congress (15-21 Oct 2007) ran on schedule; Hu's doctrine entered the Party constitution and Xi and Li were promoted in an orderly succession. Factional maneuvering (Zeng Qinghong's exit) was visible but had no documented destabilising effect.

evidence.title: 17th National Congress of the Chinese Communist Party
evidence.shows: Orderly congress; Xi and Li promoted; Scientific Development Concept enshrined; signs of maneuvering only.

verdicts.reading: Musharraf faces a political storm in 2007 that weakens him, possibly forcing him out.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D31 top risk: Musharraf is materially weakened or removed in calendar 2007.
verdicts.reason: The 2007 crisis (Chief Justice dismissal and lawyers' movement, emergency of 3 Nov, forced resignation as army chief 28 Nov, Bhutto's assassination 27 Dec) left him badly weakened; he resigned the presidency in August 2008. The 'weakened' branch occurred in the year.

evidence.title: 2007 Pakistani state of emergency
evidence.shows: Emergency, mass arrests of lawyers, Musharraf quits as army chief, Bhutto assassinated; resigns presidency Aug 2008.

verdicts.reading: Red herring: the Taiwan Strait does not become a serious source of geopolitical trouble in 2007.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D31 red herring: no cross-strait military crisis or major rupture in calendar 2007.
verdicts.reason: Chen Shui-bian's UN-membership referendum push drew protests from Beijing and Washington, but there was no military crisis; Ma Ying-jeou's March 2008 win led to a thaw.

evidence.title: Cross-Strait relations
evidence.shows: No 2007-2008 military crisis recorded; talks resumed June 2008, direct flights Dec 2008.

verdicts.reading: Red herring: North Korea does not cause serious trouble in 2007.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D31 red herring: no nuclear test, major provocation or crisis from North Korea in calendar 2007.
verdicts.reason: 2007 was a year of diplomatic progress: the 13 Feb 2007 six-party agreement, Yongbyon shut down and verified in July, disablement agreed for year end; no test until May 2009.

evidence.title: Six-party talks
evidence.shows: Feb 13 2007 deal; Yongbyon closed July 2007; no nuclear tests 2007-2008.

verdicts.reading: Red herring: Latin America (incl. Venezuela's radicalisation) does not cause serious trouble in 2007.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D31 red herring: no regional crisis with major market or geopolitical effect in calendar 2007.
verdicts.reason: Venezuela's Dec 2007 constitutional referendum was narrowly lost and Chavez conceded peacefully; markets rose. Nationalisations continued but no regional crisis materialised.

evidence.title: 2007 Venezuelan constitutional referendum
evidence.shows: 51-49 defeat accepted; protests largely peaceful; bonds and stocks rose.

verdicts.reading: Red herring: Southeast Asia does not cause serious trouble in 2007.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D31 red herring: no major political crisis in Southeast Asian states in calendar 2007.
verdicts.reason: Myanmar's Saffron Revolution (Aug-Sep 2007), the largest protests there in twenty years, was crushed with 13-31 deaths and drew US/EU sanctions; Thailand remained under post-coup military rule. Regional markets were not disrupted, so the risk materialised in part.

evidence.title: Saffron Revolution
evidence.shows: 30,000-100,000 protesters in Yangon; 13-31 deaths; ~2,900 detained; Western sanctions.

verdicts.reading: Red herring: Saudi Arabia does not become a source of serious instability in 2007.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D31 red herring: no material political or security instability in Saudi Arabia in calendar 2007.
verdicts.reason: Isolated incidents only: four French tourists killed (26 Feb 2007) and large arrests of militant cells (172 in April, 208 in November); no destabilising attack or political crisis.

evidence.title: Terrorism in Saudi Arabia
evidence.shows: 2007: one deadly attack on tourists; mass preventive arrests; no major attack.

verdicts.reading: Large aid flows start to make a meaningful difference in some of Africa's least developed states in 2007 (the feared 'basket case' risk is overstated).
verdicts.mainstream_test: D31 red herring: documented aid-driven improvement in least developed African states in 2007, rather than a deterioration.
verdicts.reason: Donor-funded HIV treatment scaled sharply: about 2.1 million people in sub-Saharan Africa were on antiretrovirals by end-2007 (30% of need), up from roughly 1.3 million a year earlier. Conflicts (Darfur, Somalia) continued but did not mark a new continent-wide deterioration.

evidence.title: Antiretrovirals reach more people in poor countries but many still lack access, UNAIDS says (Bull WHO)
evidence.shows: WHO/UNAIDS/UNICEF Towards Universal Access 2008: 2.1 million on ARVs in sub-Saharan Africa at end-2007, 30% of need.

evidence.title: UNAIDS 2008 Report on the global AIDS epidemic
evidence.shows: Documents treatment scale-up through 2007.

verdicts.reading: US politics turns inward and policy in the Bush administration and Congress moves toward protectionism in 2008.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D31 top risk: documented protectionist moves by US policymakers in calendar 2008.
verdicts.reason: Congress refused to take up the Colombia FTA through the end of 2008 and the Doha round collapsed in July 2008 with the US among the holdouts on the safeguard mechanism; but no major protectionist legislation passed in 2008 (Buy American came in 2009). Partial.

evidence.title: United States-Colombia Free Trade Agreement
evidence.shows: Not approved before the end of the 2008 Congressional session; passed only in 2011.

evidence.title: Doha Development Round
evidence.shows: Talks collapse over special safeguard mechanism; US-India/China dispute.

verdicts.reading: The Iran nuclear standoff stays dangerous in 2008 as the US pushes sanctions and Iran stays defiant.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D31 top risk: the standoff continues with new sanctions and Iranian defiance in calendar 2008.
verdicts.reason: UNSC Resolution 1803 (3 Mar 2008) added sanctions and demanded Iran halt enrichment; Iran refused and continued enrichment. No strike, consistent with the summary.

evidence.title: UN Security Council Resolution 1803
evidence.shows: Third sanctions resolution; Iran required to cease enrichment.

verdicts.reading: Frustration with stalled politics jeopardises Iraq's central government in 2008, even if security improves.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D31 top risk: Iraq's central government is materially weakened or threatened by political deadlock in calendar 2008.
verdicts.reason: The opposite happened: the Basra operation (Mar 2008) consolidated Maliki's authority with cross-sectarian support, and the government passed the SOFA through cabinet and parliament in November 2008.

evidence.title: Battle of Basra (2008)
evidence.shows: Operation strengthened Maliki's central authority.

evidence.title: U.S.-Iraq Status of Forces Agreement
evidence.shows: Parliament ratified SOFA 149 of 275, showing a functioning though divided government.

verdicts.reading: A mass-casualty terrorist attack by Al Qaeda or allied groups remains a substantial risk in 2008.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D31 top risk: a mass-casualty jihadist attack occurs in calendar 2008.
verdicts.reason: Lashkar-e-Taiba's Mumbai attacks (26-29 Nov 2008) killed 166 civilians; the Islamabad Marriott bombing (20 Sep 2008) killed 54.

evidence.title: 2008 Mumbai attacks
evidence.shows: 166 civilians killed by LeT gunmen.

evidence.title: Islamabad Marriott Hotel bombing
evidence.shows: 54 killed.

verdicts.reading: Afghanistan and Pakistan face serious, worsening political and security problems and Islamist radicalism in 2008.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D31 top risk: security and political conditions deteriorate in both countries in calendar 2008.
verdicts.reason: Afghan civilian deaths rose about 40% to 2,118, the highest since 2001; in Pakistan Musharraf resigned (Aug 2008) and the Marriott bombing killed 54.

evidence.title: Civilian casualties in the war in Afghanistan
evidence.shows: UNAMA: 1,523 (2007) to 2,118 (2008) civilian deaths.

evidence.title: Islamabad Marriott Hotel bombing
evidence.shows: Major attack in Pakistan's capital.

verdicts.reading: An emboldened Kremlin acts as a spoiler on key international issues in 2008, opposing US unilateralism.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D31 top risk: Russia materially obstructs or confronts the West on major international issues in calendar 2008.
verdicts.reason: Russia went to war with Georgia (Aug 2008) and recognised Abkhazia and South Ossetia (26 Aug), beyond a spoiler role; it also opposed Kosovo's independence.

evidence.title: Russo-Georgian War
evidence.shows: Russian invasion of Georgia; recognition of breakaway regions on 26 Aug 2008.

verdicts.reading: The Mbeki-Zuma split makes 2008 a difficult, uncertain year for South Africa, though the country largely weathers it.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D31 top risk: the ANC-government split produces a material political crisis in calendar 2008.
verdicts.reason: The split came to a head: the ANC recalled Mbeki, who resigned on 20 Sep 2008 and was replaced by Motlanthe; the transition was constitutional. The risk materialised (more sharply than the quote's expectation that Mbeki would stay to 2009).

evidence.title: Thabo Mbeki
evidence.shows: Mbeki resigns after ANC NEC recall; Motlanthe succeeds.

verdicts.reading: The AKP's constitutional plans raise Turkey's risk of political instability in 2008 and distract from its EU bid.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D31 top risk: a material political/constitutional crisis over the AKP agenda in calendar 2008.
verdicts.reason: After the headscarf amendment, the chief prosecutor sought to close the ruling AKP; the Constitutional Court on 30 Jul 2008 fell one vote short of closure but cut its funding and found it a centre of anti-secular activity.

evidence.title: 2008 Justice and Development Party closure trial
evidence.shows: Ruling party survives closure by one vote; state funding halved.

verdicts.reading: Energy policy failures and underinvestment in Latin America limit regional growth in 2008.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D31 top risk: documented energy shortages with economic effect in Latin American countries in calendar 2008.
verdicts.reason: Chile suffered a double energy crisis in 2007-2008 as Argentine gas exports fell to about 1 Mcm/day in 2008, and Argentina kept rationing gas; but the region's 2008 growth slowdown came from the global crisis, and the effect was limited to some countries.

evidence.title: IEA Energy Policy Review 2009: Chile
evidence.shows: Chile's 2007-2008 energy crisis from Argentine gas cuts and drought.

evidence.title: 2004 Argentine energy crisis
evidence.shows: Argentine gas export restrictions to Chile recurring through the late 2000s.

verdicts.reading: Red herring: China remains stable in 2008.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D31 red herring: no material domestic instability in China in calendar 2008.
verdicts.reason: Regime and economy stayed stable through the Olympics, but the March 2008 Tibetan unrest (about 150-235 protests, 23 to 200+ deaths, troops deployed, journalists expelled) was a significant bout of instability. Materialised in part.

evidence.title: 2008 Tibetan unrest
evidence.shows: Widespread Tibetan protests and riots with deaths and a large security response.

verdicts.reading: Red herring: Taiwan remains stable in 2008.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D31 red herring: no cross-strait crisis in calendar 2008.
verdicts.reason: Ma Ying-jeou won in March 2008; semi-official talks resumed in June and direct flights began in December.

evidence.title: Cross-Strait relations
evidence.shows: Thaw after Ma's election; talks and direct flights.

verdicts.reading: Red herring: North Korea is not a source of serious instability in 2008.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D31 red herring: no nuclear test or major crisis from North Korea in calendar 2008.
verdicts.reason: No nuclear test in 2008; the US removed North Korea from the terrorism list in October 2008. Verification talks stalled, but no crisis.

evidence.title: Six-party talks

verdicts.reading: Red herring: Saudi Arabia remains stable in 2008.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D31 red herring: no material political or security instability in Saudi Arabia in calendar 2008.
verdicts.reason: No significant attack or political crisis recorded in 2008.

evidence.title: Terrorism in Saudi Arabia

verdicts.reading: Red herring: Nigeria is not a material source of instability in 2008.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D31 red herring: no material instability in Nigeria (politics or oil supply) in calendar 2008.
verdicts.reason: National politics were stable, but MEND's Niger Delta campaign hit hard: the Bonga attack (20 Jun 2008) shut about 200,000 b/d, a May pipeline attack halted 170,000 b/d, and an 'oil war' was declared in September. Materialised in part.

evidence.title: Movement for the Emancipation of the Niger Delta
evidence.shows: Bonga offshore attack, pipeline attacks and Sept 2008 'oil war'.

verdicts.reading: Red herring: Russia's domestic politics stay stable in 2008 through the succession.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D31 red herring: no material domestic political instability in Russia in calendar 2008.
verdicts.reason: Medvedev won on 2 Mar 2008 with 71% and appointed Putin prime minister; a managed, stable succession (unfair by observers' standards, but not unstable).

evidence.title: 2008 Russian presidential election
evidence.shows: Medvedev elected; Putin becomes PM; continuity.

verdicts.reading: A strengthened Congress drives the US economic-policy and financial-regulation agenda in 2009.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D31 top risk: Congress materially drives major economic/financial-regulation legislation in calendar 2009.
verdicts.reason: Congress wrote and passed the $787bn stimulus (Feb 2009) and the House passed the Frank Wall Street Reform bill on 11 Dec 2009 (223-202), with Dodd's Senate draft introduced the same month; the law followed in July 2010.

evidence.title: Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act
evidence.shows: House passed the Frank bill 11 Dec 2009; Dodd and Frank drove the reform.

verdicts.reading: Security in India, Pakistan and Afghanistan deteriorates significantly in 2009 and draws the US and Europe more deeply into conflicts there.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D31 top risk: documented security deterioration in all three named countries plus deeper Western involvement in calendar 2009; partial if only some.
verdicts.reason: Pakistan's conflict deaths rose from 6,683 (2008) to 11,317 (2009); Afghan civilian deaths rose 14% to 2,412 and the US announced a surge. India did not deteriorate: its conflict deaths fell from 2,605 to 2,263. Two of three countries.

evidence.title: SATP: Fatalities in terrorist violence in Pakistan
Civilian casualties in the war in Afghanistan
evidence.shows: UNAMA 2,412 civilian deaths in 2009, +14%.

verdicts.reading: 2009 is the critical year for Iran-Israel conflict, direct or through proxies, as Iran nears bomb capacity.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D31 top risk: direct or proxy armed conflict between Iran and Israel occurs in calendar 2009.
verdicts.reason: Proxy conflict occurred only at the year's start: Israel's Gaza war against Hamas ran 27 Dec 2008 to 18 Jan 2009 (about 1,166-1,417 Palestinian deaths), with reported strikes on Iranian arms shipments. No direct Israel-Iran conflict and no strike in 2009.

evidence.title: Gaza War (2008-2009)
evidence.shows: War against Hamas through 18 Jan 2009; Israeli attack on an Iranian arms ship reported.

verdicts.reading: The financial crisis brings increased social unrest in Russia, met with near-zero tolerance for dissent, and worse relations with the West.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D31 top risk: materially increased crisis-driven social unrest in Russia in calendar 2009 (and worsening ties with the West).
verdicts.reason: Some unrest occurred, e.g. the Pikalyovo highway blockade over unpaid wages that brought Putin in person (June 2009), but no wave of unrest; relations with the West improved under the 'reset' (from March 2009). Part of the risk materialised.

evidence.title: Pikalyovo, Leningrad Oblast
evidence.shows: Residents block highway over wage arrears; Putin orders payment.

evidence.title: Russian reset
evidence.shows: US-Russia relations improved in 2009: transit deal, missile-defence shift.

verdicts.reading: Iraq's government faces a series of political tests in 2009 (elections, US withdrawal) that determine whether it can keep the country united and stable.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D31 top risk: the tests produce a material destabilisation of Iraq or its government in calendar 2009.
verdicts.reason: The tests came and the government held: provincial elections on 31 Jan 2009 were the most peaceful since 2003 and strengthened Maliki; US troops left the cities in June. But mass-casualty bombings struck government ministries (19 Aug: 101 dead; more in Oct and Dec). Risk materialised in part.

evidence.title: 2009 Iraqi governorate elections
evidence.shows: Peaceful, Iraqi-secured election; State of Law wins.

evidence.title: 19 August 2009 Baghdad bombings
evidence.shows: 101 killed in attacks on Foreign and Finance ministries.

verdicts.reading: Chavez's referendum to abolish term limits is unlikely to succeed in 2009, and he turns more authoritarian.

evidence.title: 2009 Venezuelan constitutional referendum

verdicts.reading: Rising narco violence and corruption in 2009 raise questions about Mexico's strategy against organised crime.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D31 top risk: drug-related violence rises materially in calendar 2009.
verdicts.reason: Drug-war deaths rose from 6,290 (2008) to 9,724 (2009) and kept climbing (15,273 in 2010).

verdicts.reading: The secularist-Islamist fight in Turkey becomes a serious obstacle to economic advancement and the EU bid in 2009.

evidence.title: July 2009 Urumqi riots

verdicts.reading: Red herring: low oil prices do not produce political instability in the Gulf monarchies in 2009.

evidence.title: Dubai World

evidence.title: 2009 Iranian presidential election protests
